assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform where flat bands give superconductivity and correlated insulators in a tunable, clean material. The theoretical flat-band prediction followed by experiment is the kind of theory-to-measurement link I value, and it follows the surprises of 2D crystals.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive flat-band prediction at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting states. Three names fit the supplied credit, though the experimental side involved a larger team and Cao, as first author, is not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many groups worldwide within a few years and explained by continuum band theory that agrees with spectroscopy. Still maturing, since the superconducting pairing mechanism is debated, but the central discovery is solid and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled.
Credit between theory pair and the experimental group, and Cao's role, could be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new classification of electronic states, protected by time-reversal symmetry and not by broken symmetry. It is conceptually deep, quantitatively predictive and has lasting influence across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group made the HgTe quantum well measurement that confirmed edge transport. Hasan and others made 3D observations (ARPES), so a trio of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is the cleanest fit within the credited names, but excludes the 3D branch and others such as Zhang and Bernevig.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by transport and by spectroscopy (ARPES), with theory that matches well. The field is mature, and 2016 recognised the earlier topological-phase work, so a follow-on prize is plausible and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and how the committee views it.
Prediction credit for HgTe (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and the 3D branch lies outside this configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, then giant TMR in MgO junctions, supplies the reading mechanism of modern hard-disk heads and magnetic memory. It is a clear experimental discovery with huge practical consequences, and it builds on spin-dependent tunnelling that theory can explain.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group and, in parallel, Yuasa and colleagues, found giant TMR in MgO. The credited names support a fair three-person prize for the discovery, but the MgO-stage credit is split and Yuasa and others are not included.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed, with first-principles theory of coherent tunnelling (Butler, Mathon) agreeing with experiment, and commercially deployed for two decades. Long overdue rather than premature, though 2007 GMR recognition overlaps in subject.
uncertainties: Credit for MgO giant TMR is shared with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the central modern framework for strongly correlated electrons, giving a controlled non-perturbative account of the Mott transition and, combined with DFT, material-specific predictions. It is original, quantitative and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar formulated DMFT and its impurity-model mapping. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt is a plausible trio, but Metzner is not credited, so some contribution would go unrecognised.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and validation, including DFT+DMFT for real materials and comparison with cold-atom and spectroscopic data. Mature, but as a theory prize it depends on whether the committee wants a method as the centre.
uncertainties: Metzner's role in the original limit is not covered by the credited names.
A methods and theory prize needs a clear physical discovery as the centre.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx in 2008 revealed a second family of high-Tc materials, with multiband magnetism-linked pairing. It is a clear materials discovery with large follow-up.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono made the discovery in the Hosono group; subsequent rapid raising of Tc in China (Chen, Ren, Wang) is arguably separate. The two credited names are a fair, compact configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced within weeks and extensively studied by neutron and photoemission spectroscopy. The pairing mechanism remains unresolved and Tc does not exceed the cuprates, so the practical impact is limited.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the Chinese groups that raised Tc is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with the magic-wavelength idea, reached about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty and enabled tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a candidate redefinition of the second. It is clean, quantitative and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye led the strontium clock to the highest accuracy and stability. The two-name configuration is natural and fair, with Hall and Hänsch already honoured in 2005 for the comb.
assessment.maturity: Independently achieved by many national laboratories and compared across continents. Mature enough for recognition, though the redefinition of the second is pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
Ion-clock contributions (e.g. Al+ clocks) are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in transmission electron microscopy delivered sub-angstrom imaging and atomic-resolution spectroscopy, which materials and condensed matter research now routinely uses. The invention overcame a limit long thought fundamental (Scherzer), with enormous instrumentation impact.
assessment.attribution: Rose developed the correction theory; Haider and Urban implemented the hexapole corrector for TEM; Krivanek's STEM corrector is a parallel strand not in the list. The credited trio is a coherent core configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well established and widely adopted, so recognition is timely and reproducible. Instrument prizes are accepted by the committee, but the physics discovery element is weaker than for materials discoveries.
uncertainties: Krivanek and Dellby for STEM correction are outside the credited names.
Whether an instrument invention counts as a physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intrinsic magnetism in atomically thin van der Waals crystals (CrI3, Cr2Ge2Te6) showed long-range order survives in two dimensions with anisotropy, against the Mermin-Wagner expectation without anisotropy. It connects directly to spin theory and has spawned a wide field of 2D magnets.
assessment.attribution: The 2017 CrI3 and Cr2Ge2Te6 papers came from Xu's and Zhang's groups. Jarillo-Herrero is better known for the moire work, and his role in the magnetism discovery may be weaker. The credit as supplied is not obviously clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in several laboratories and understood with first-principles and spin-model theory, but application and the field are younger, so recognition may be premature relative to the other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether Jarillo-Herrero belongs in a 2D magnetism prize.
Younger field, with the long-term role still open.
